title: Two Kinds of Sound
logline: Where the day's catch is landed in the open wind, auctioneers' calls compete with gusts and surf, and buyers lean in and watch hands to be sure of a number.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The elements in the potter's hands move out to the wind of an eastern landing site, where a voice has to be told apart from the weather.

thread_out.thread: From an ear straining against the wind to eyes waiting behind dressings: a free eye camp, and first sight arriving after months.

requirements: An active fish auction on an open, windy beach or landing site
Fishers, auctioneers and buyers willing to be filmed at their real work
Enough wind on the day to make the sound contrast real, not staged

suggestions.why: The east coast has open, often windy beach landing sites with beach-based auctions.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A shouted bid and a gust of wind are the same kind of thing to the ear: sound. The texts say one is made by a mind that means something, and the other only by the weather.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කෑගසා කියන මිලක හඬත් සුළං හඬත් කනට එකම ආකාරයේ ශබ්දයක් වුවද, එකක් යමක් කියන්නට සිතන සිතකින්ද අනෙක කාලගුණයෙන් පමණක්ද හටගන්නා බව අභිධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts sort the twenty-eight kinds of matter by which of the four origins can produce them, and sound is the one kind that comes from exactly two: mind and temperature. A speaking voice is mind-born, arising when the air produced by a thought to speak strikes the places where sound is formed, while the noise of wind is temperature-born. Sound is one of the five sense objects, a derived kind of matter that depends on the four great elements, and the Margaya describes it as arising from striking and bursting and not lasting long as a series.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: On the open beach the soundtrack carries the distinction: calls and bids rise and are swallowed by gusts and surf, and buyers lean in, cup their ears and ask for a number again. The viewer comes to hear two kinds of sound side by side, one trying to say something and one that is not, without the film ever explaining which is which.
lesson.caution: 'Temperature' here means the heat element as a producing condition, not simply the weather, and the texts' account of sound should not be presented as an early version of acoustics.
lesson.builds_on: The potter's clay showed the elements under the hand; this film turns to what the ear receives, and to the fact that the same kind of matter can come from different makers: a mind that means something, or the weather.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
